To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
changes in the expression levels in circulating cancer stem cells in colon cancer patients may predict response to therapy.

the expression levels of CD133, SOXT1 and TWIST1 may be associated with the response to treatment, and the expression levels of OCT4 and TWIS1 may be associated to the relapse of the tumor after treatment.

changes in the expression levels and the correlation between the expression levels of different stem cell surface markers in the peripheral circulation of colorectal cancer patients may predict the clinical outcome.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the prognostic value of the expression of the stem cell markers CD133, OCT-4, SOX-2 and TWIST-1 in the peripheral blood in colon cancer.
the prognostic value of stem cell markers and may contribute to a better understanding of the behavior of colon cancer.
the expression of stemness markers in the peripheral circulating tumor cells in colon cancer patients and the prognostic value of this expression in the response to treatment.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
CD133, TWIST1, SOX2 or OCT4 expression in the peripheral blood may be a prognostic marker in patients with colon cancer.
the expression of the stem cell markers CD133, OCT3/4, TWIST1, SOX2 is a prognostic indicator for colon cancer.
the expression of the markers CD134, SOX2 OCT4 and TWITS1 has a prognostic value in colon cancer.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
stem cell markers expression in the peripheral blood may be used to predict the behavior of colon cancer.

the expression of stemness markers may be used as a prognostic marker of response in patients with colon cancer, and that the correlation between the expression levels of CD133 and TWIT1 may be associated with the tumor regrowth and the metastatic relapse of patients.

the expression of the stem cell markers CD133, OCT, SOX and TWIST in the peripheral blood may have a prognostic role in the response to treatment and in predicting the relapse of metastasis in colon cancer patients.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the evaluation of the stem cell gene expression pattern in the peripheral blood may be a useful tool for predicting response to chemotherapy.
the expression of CD133, SOx2, OCT4 or TWIST1 can serve as prognostic markers for colon cancer.
the expression of stemness markers in the peripheral circulating blood of patients with colorectal cancer may be used as a prognostic marker for the prediction of the response to chemotherapy.
